actions.rule: Pursuant to the Charter, no later than the day following final passage or adoption by the Board, the Clerk of the Board (Clerk) shall transmit to the Mayor ordinances and resolutions with the record of Supervisors who voted for or against the legislation or were absent or excused. Within 10 calendar days of receipt of legislation, the Mayor shall return the legislation to the Clerk of the Board. If the 10th day is a weekday, the Mayor has until 5:00 p.m. on that day to return legislation. If the 10th day is a weekend, the Mayor, attested by a witness, must sign legislation by midnight on the 10th day and return to Clerk of the Board on the following Monday by 8:00 a.m. The Mayor has three choices in accordance with Board Rule 2.14 : Sign the legislation, in which case it becomes law in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of legislation. Return the legislation unsigned, in which case the legislation becomes law at the end of the 10-day period for consideration by the Mayor in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of legislation. If the Mayor informs the Clerk in writing that he or she is waiving the remainder of the 10-day period, then the legislation is deemed approved on the date the Clerk receives the written waiver. Disapprove and veto the legislation, in which case the Board may override the veto and approve the legislation within 30 days by an affirmative vote of not less than two-thirds of the full Board, eight votes in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of the legislation.

Following its final passage by the Board of Supervisors on September 15, 2026, the street tree ordinance (File 251211) moves to the Mayor for review. 

Under the San Francisco Charter, the Clerk of the Board transmits the ordinance to the Mayor, who then has 10 calendar days from receipt to take action. The Mayor may:
- **Sign the legislation**, enacting it into law.
- **Return it unsigned**, allowing it to become law automatically at the end of the 10-day period (or upon written waiver).
- **Veto the legislation**, returning it to the Board, which would need at least eight votes within 30 days to override the veto.
On September 15, 2026, the Board finally passed File 251211 in a 7-4 vote, triggering Mayoral review.

If the 10th day is a weekday, the Mayor has until 5:00 p.m. on that day to return legislation. If the 10th day is a weekend, the Mayor, attested by a witness, must sign legislation by midnight on the 10th day and return to Clerk of the Board on the following Monday by 8:00 a.m. The Mayor has three choices in accordance with Board Rule 2.14 : Sign the legislation, in which case it becomes law in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of legislation. Return the legislation unsigned, in which case the legislation becomes law at the end of the 10-day period for consideration by the Mayor in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of legislation. If the Mayor informs the Clerk in writing that he or she is waiving the remainder of the 10-day period, then the legislation is deemed approved on the date the Clerk receives the written waiver. Disapprove and veto the legislation, in which case the Board may override the veto and approve the legislation within 30 days by an affirmative vote of not less than two-thirds of the full Board, eight votes in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of the legislation.

rows.summary: The Board considered the Consolidated Budget and Appropriation Ordinance for City and County departments for FYs 2026-2027 and 2027-2028. The measure was considered alongside the entire annual budget package and passed on first reading.

rows.item_title: Resolution Adjusting the Access Line Tax with the Consumer Price Index of 2026
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution concurring with the Controller's adjustment of the Access Line Tax to match the Consumer Price Index for 2026. The resolution was adopted without objection as part of the budget package.

rows.item_title: Accept and Expend Grant - Friends of San Francisco Public Library - Chinatown Branch Renovation Capital Project - FYs 2026-2027 through 2029-2030 - Up to $1,500,000 of In-Kind Gifts, Services, and Cash Monies
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution authorizing the Public Library to accept and expend an in-kind and cash grant of up to $1.5 million from the Friends of the San Francisco Public Library for Chinatown Branch renovations. The resolution was adopted as part of the budget package.

rows.item_title: Accept and Expend Grants - Recurring State Grant Funds - Department of Public Health - FY2026-2027
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution authorizing the Department of Public Health to accept and expend recurring state grant funds for FY 2026-2027. The resolution was adopted as part of the annual budget package.

rows.item_title: Various Codes - Streamlining Reporting Requirements and Procedures, Removing Obsolete Programs and Requirements, and Other Code Cleanup
rows.summary: The Board voted on final reading of an ordinance modifying numerous reporting requirements, removing obsolete programs, and making code cleanups across city codes. The ordinance passed 7-4, with Supervisors Walton, Chan, Fielder, and Melgar dissenting.

rows.item_title: Planning, Administrative, Building Codes - Inclusionary Housing Program Updates and Reductions; Development Impact Fee Reductions
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending the Planning, Building, and Administrative Codes to reduce inclusionary affordable housing requirements and development impact fees. The ordinance was finally passed on a 9-2 vote, with Supervisors Walton and Chen voting no.

rows.item_title: Administrative Code - Expanding Drug-Free Permanent Supportive Housing

rows.summary: The Board approved on first reading an ordinance adjusting Sheriff's Office appropriations by $14 million to cover overtime costs in FY 2025-2026. All three resolutions were adopted without objection.

rows.summary: The Board retroactively approved an amendment to the Joint Exercise of Powers Agreement between the SFPUC, the City of Brisbane, and the Guadalupe Valley Municipal Improvement District for sewer services through 2027. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.summary: The Board approved a purchase and sale agreement with PG&E to acquire real property at 5000 Hunters Point Boulevard for $575,000 for the Recreation and Parks Department. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Grant of Easement - Pacific Gas and Electric Company - Execution of an Easement and Installation of a High-Voltage Transmission Line - John McLaren Park - $950,000
rows.summary: The Board approved an agreement granting PG&E a subsurface utility easement in John McLaren Park for $950,000 to install a high-voltage transmission line. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Accept and Expend In-Kind Gift - Consulting Services - FUSE Corp - FUSE Fellows Program - Valued at $2,520,000
rows.summary: The Board authorized the Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development to accept an in-kind gift of consulting services valued at $2,520,000 from FUSE Corp for seven fellows to strengthen health, housing, and homelessness systems. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Real Property Lease - JPPF 1300 Battery, L.P. - 1300 Battery Street - $1,498,012.50 Total Base Rent
rows.summary: The Board approved a Port Commission lease with JPPF 1300 Battery for restaurant space and outdoor dining at 1300 Battery Street through 2046 with total base rent of approximately $1.5 million. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Management Agreement Amendment - Pasha Automotive Services - Pier 80 Terminal - Discontinue $50,000 Monthly Fee - Revised Revenue Sharing
rows.summary: The Board authorized the Port to amend its management agreement with Pasha Automotive Services for the Pier 80 Terminal, discontinuing a $50,000 monthly fee and revising revenue sharing terms. The resolution was adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Amended Loan Agreement - 1234 Great Highway LLC - 1234, 1270, and 1280 Great Highway - 100% Affordable Housing - Not to Exceed $27,248,500
Ground Lease - Mercy Housing California 109, L.P. - 1939 Market Street - 100% Affordable Housing - $15,000 Annual Base Rent
rows.summary: The Board approved a pre-development loan amendment of up to $27 million for affordable senior housing on Great Highway and a 75-year ground lease with Mercy Housing for 187 units of 100% affordable housing at 1939 Market Street. Both resolutions were adopted without objection.

rows.item_title: Planning Code - Hotel Uses in RH, RM, and RTO Districts
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending the Planning Code to increase the allowable guest rooms for conditional-use hotels in RH, RM, and RTO districts from five to ten rooms. The ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Public Works Code - Banner Fee Waiver
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending the Public Works Code to waive banner and inspection fees for certain nonprofit organizations in neighborhood commercial and transit-oriented districts. The ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Fire, Public Works Codes - Audit Amnesty Fee Waivers
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance amending the Fire and Public Works Codes to waive review and processing fees to abate violations under the Department of Building Inspection's audit amnesty program. The ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Police Code - Penalties for Prohibited Discharge of Fireworks
rows.summary: The Board debated an ordinance amending the Police Code to establish fines for the unlawful discharge of fireworks, setting infraction fines of $125 to $250 for first offenses and misdemeanor penalties for repeat violations within five years. Sponsor Alan Wong argued local citations are necessary to deter dangerous fireworks activity, while Jackie Fielder opposed the measure over potential jail time for minor infractions. The ordinance passed on first reading by a 9-2 vote.

rows.item_title: 7 SPECIAL ORDER 2:30 P.M. - Recognition of Commendations
rows.summary: The Board held its special commendations order honoring outstanding community leaders and organizations. Honorees included Mary Lindy upon her retirement as CEO of Heritage on the Marina, Mark Campbell and Art with Elders, Adult and Juvenile Probation Department staff, Aberdeen Fight Club and coach JP Peterson, community leader Damien Posey of Us4Us, retiring JCCCNC executive director Paul Osaki, and Lee Housekeeper for organizing 37 years of the 1906 Earthquake and Fire Commemoration.

rows.item_title: Hearing - Appeal of Determination of Exemption from Environmental Review - Proposed 1200 Larkin Street Project
rows.summary: The Board announced that the project sponsor had withdrawn their project application for 1200 Larkin Street and the Planning Department had rescinded its approval letter. The environmental review appeal was declared moot and the Board took no action.

Following extensive testimony and public comment, the hearing was filed.

rows.item_title: Hearing - Committee of the Whole - Downtown Community Benefit District - Renewal and Expansion - July 21, 2026, at 3:00 p.m.
rows.summary: The Board convened as a Committee of the Whole to hold a public hearing on the renewal and expansion of the Downtown Community Benefit District to a 10-year term covering 70 blocks. City staff, property owners, and business leaders voiced support for expanded clean and safe operations and Embarcadero Park activation, while other commenters questioned surveillance and homeless outreach policies. The hearing was filed pending the counting of weighted ballots.

rows.item_title: Resolution to Establish - Downtown Community Benefit District
rows.summary: The Board considered a resolution to establish the renewed and expanded Downtown Community Benefit District and order the levy of property assessments for a ten-year term. Final action on the resolution was paused while the Department of Elections completed the ballot tabulation.

rows.item_title: Police Code - Lending Books to Individuals Under 21 Years Old
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance repealing an obsolete Police Code section that prohibited circulating libraries from lending or renting books or pamphlets to people under 21 without written parental consent. Sponsor Alan Wong noted the law was identified through his office's 'Dumb Laws Contest,' and the ordinance passed on first reading unanimously.

rows.item_title: Health Code - Code Cleanup
rows.summary: The Board considered an ordinance repealing outdated Health Code provisions that banned carrying bread in open baskets on city streets and regulated commercial wiping rags. Sponsor Alan Wong explained that modern health standards supersede these archaic rules, and the ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

rows.item_title: Liquor License Issuance - 284 Noe Street - The Love Potion Library LLC
rows.summary: The Board approved a resolution determining that the issuance of a Type 42 on-sale beer and wine liquor license to The Love Potion Library LLC at 284 Noe Street would serve the public convenience or necessity. The resolution was adopted without objection.

actions.rule: Pursuant to the Charter, no later than the day following final passage or adoption by the Board, the Clerk of the Board (Clerk) shall transmit to the Mayor ordinances and resolutions with the record of Supervisors who voted for or against the legislation or were absent or excused. Within 10 calendar days of receipt of legislation, the Mayor shall return the legislation to the Clerk of the Board. If the 10th day is a weekday, the Mayor has until 5:00 p.m. on that day to return legislation. If the 10th day is a weekend, the Mayor, attested by a witness, must sign legislation by midnight on the 10th day and return to Clerk of the Board on the following Monday by 8:00 a.m. The Mayor has three choices in accordance with Board Rule 2.14 : Sign the legislation, in which case it becomes law in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of legislation. Return the legislation unsigned, in which case the legislation becomes law at the end of the 10-day period for consideration by the Mayor in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of legislation. If the Mayor informs the Clerk in writing that he or she is waiving the remainder of the 10-day period, then the legislation is deemed approved on the date the Clerk receives the written waiver. Disapprove and veto the legislation, in which case the Board may override the veto and approve the legislation within 30 days by an affirmative vote of not less than two-thirds of the full Board, eight votes in accordance with Board Rule 2.16 relating to the effective date of the legislation.

Supervisor Dorsey introduced an amendment for the Board to consent to the removal, arguing the Charter grants the mayor appointment authority over at-will commissioners. The Board approved the amendment and consented to the removal on a 9-2 vote, with Supervisors Melgar and Fielder dissenting.

MATCH (entry)-[:CONCERNS]->(:Legislation {file_no: $file_no})
OPTIONAL MATCH (entry)-[:PART_OF]->(parent:Item)

       i.outcome AS outcome,

        no: sum(CASE WHEN v.vote = 'no' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),
        absent: sum(CASE WHEN v.vote = 'absent' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END),

ORDER BY date, start_sec LIMIT 100
